dispositions.external_claim_scope: LangGraph issue #8115 and current pinned put_writes code shape
dispositions.factory_action: Retain the executable fixture as a recurrence test candidate; require expected-write-set equality and one atomic critical section for any shared in-process result collector.
dispositions.mechanism: Parallel writers publish stale snapshots by read-filter-rebind-append and silently erase sibling checkpoint writes.
dispositions.why: The abstract pattern is deterministically reproduced and the locked control passes, but this unit did not establish current LangGraph's actual concurrent call path or run an end-to-end LangGraph graph.

dispositions.external_claim_scope: LangGraph persistence documentation, Anthropic engineering retrospective, and GitHub workflow artifact documentation
dispositions.factory_action: Retain the existing PO-03 rule that provider completion cannot advance custody without a durable result plus hash verification and immutable read-back. This subordinate made no shared-control edit.
dispositions.mechanism: A worker reports completion while its result exists only in process-local memory; process loss removes the result although the completion receipt survives.
dispositions.why: The memory-only path produced 12 provider-completed receipts and zero durable read-backs; the atomic-file control produced 12 of 12 hash-verified read-backs.

dispositions.external_claim_scope: Cursor 2026-08-18 GitHub-connected Cloud Agent workflow incident
dispositions.factory_action: Use only as current provider-failure context; do not use it to infer result loss or a recovery mechanism.
dispositions.why: The incident reports failures and rate-limit errors but no root cause, completed-result loss, or custody read-back evidence.

hypothesis_disposition.statement: Published sources reveal at least two result-loss mechanisms reproducible as sanitized local factory invariants: stale concurrent rebind can erase writes, and provider completion without durable storage can leave no recoverable result. The sources do not establish provider- or framework-level incidence rates.
